session.summary: The user outlines a project called 'Follow The Money' (FTFM) focused on creating a system to track, store, and analyze statements made in news and podcasts. The concept involves extracting entities and claims from media sources to create a structured record of public statements, promises, and contradictions to promote accountability. The user details technical implementation ideas including JSON structures, embeddings, and a RAG system.

records.content: The 'Follow The Money' (FTFM) project aims to create a system that tracks and analyzes statements from news sources and podcasts. The core concept is building a fact-tracking database that serves as a source of truth, allowing easy verification of statements made by public figures and tracking how their positions evolve over time.

details.title: Follow The Money Project Overview
details.notes: This appears to be a core project concept that needs further refinement. The user seems particularly interested in creating transparency in media and politics.

project.goal: Create a system that tracks and analyzes statements from media sources to promote accountability

records.content: For an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) of the FTFM project, consider mapping all episodes of Glenn Greenwald's podcasts over the last six months. This would involve extracting all named entities and claims, with references to the exact moment each claim was made. This approach could then be expanded to include additional media sources.

details.title: MVP Concept for FTFM
details.notes: Starting with a single podcast host would allow for testing the concept with a manageable dataset before scaling to additional sources.

project.goal: Create a functioning prototype using Glenn Greenwald's podcasts as source material

records.content: The FTFM system would function as society's 'storage layer' for tracking real-world events and statements - something currently missing from our information ecosystem. Unlike Wikipedia, which focuses on static, historical information, this system would track dynamic, evolving narratives and statements made by public figures.

details.title: FTFM as Society's Storage Layer
details.notes: This concept positions the project as filling a significant gap in our information infrastructure. There's a philosophical dimension here about the nature of truth and record-keeping that might be worth exploring.

project.goal: Develop a system that records and makes accessible dynamic real-world statements and events

records.content: The FTFM system would detect and flag significant events, such as when a politician makes a promise (e.g., 'I will do X on my first day in office'). These would be tagged as events or promises, and the system would track whether those promises are fulfilled. This creates a mechanism for identifying patterns in behavior and statements over time.

details.title: Promise and Pattern Tracking Feature
details.notes: This functionality would be particularly valuable during election cycles and for long-term accountability of elected officials.

project.goal: Develop an automated system to track promises made by public figures and flag fulfillment or non-fulfillment

records.content: The technical architecture for FTFM involves creating a model to batch process transcripts into structured JSON records containing entities (people, places, laws, events) and their relationships. Special attention would be paid to conflicts of interest, hypocrisies, and changes in stated positions. Each record would include embeddings for semantic search capabilities.

details.title: Technical Architecture
details.notes: The technical implementation will require advanced NLP capabilities, particularly for identifying contradictions and changes in position over time.

project.goal: Design and implement the technical architecture for the FTFM system

records.content: The FTFM system would include a translation layer that converts JSON structures from the database into markdown notes and files that can be viewed and edited in Obsidian. This would require a syncing mechanism between the backend database and the front-end Obsidian notes to maintain consistency across both systems.

details.title: FTFM Integration with Obsidian
details.notes: This integration would make the data more accessible to users familiar with note-taking tools while maintaining the structured database backend for more complex operations.

project.goal: Create a bi-directional sync between JSON database and Obsidian markdown files

records.content: The final component of the FTFM system would be a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline that allows users to query the database. A generative AI would analyze the data, conduct research, and answer questions based on the information stored in the system, creating a powerful tool for fact-checking and analysis.

details.title: RAG Query System
details.notes: This would be the user-facing component that makes the data actionable and useful for journalists, researchers, and the general public.

project.goal: Build a RAG system to allow intuitive querying of the FTFM database

records.content: Obtain transcripts for one or two of Glenn Greenwald's podcasts as initial test data for the FTFM project.

details.title: Acquire Glenn Greenwald Podcast Transcripts
details.notes: This is a necessary first step to begin testing the entity extraction and JSON conversion process.

project.goal: Gather initial test data for FTFM prototype development
